title: Towards a knowledge-enhanced single-cell foundation model
abstract: arXiv:2609.14970v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Single-cell foundation models (scFMs) increasingly rely on large-scale transcriptomic pretraining, yet expanding pretraining data can yield diminishing gains while substantially increasing computational cost. Our data scaling analyses showed that incorporating biological knowledge, including cell-level text annotation and gene-level regulatory information, provided additional scaling dimension than simply increasing data size. Motivated by this observation, we present scKITE, a simple yet effective scFM that integrates cell-annotation and gene-regulatory supervision into a shared transcriptomic Transformer encoder through lightweight auxiliary decoders. These decoders are used only during pretraining and subsequently discarded, yielding a general-purpose encoder enriched with biological knowledge for downstream applications. translated_title: 迈向知识增强的单细胞基础模型
translated_abstract: 单细胞基础模型日益依赖大规模转录组数据的预训练，然而不断扩大预训练数据规模的收益正在递减，同时还会显著增加计算成本。我们的数据规模分析表明，引入生物学知识——包括细胞层面的文本注释和基因层面的调控信息——相比单纯增加数据规模，提供了额外的扩展维度。基于这一观察，我们提出了scKITE，一个简单而有效的单细胞基础模型，它通过轻量级的辅助解码器将细胞注释和基因调控监督信息整合到共享的转录组Transformer编码器中。这些辅助解码器仅在预训练阶段使用，随后被丢弃，从而得到一个融合了生物学知识的通用编码器，可用于下游应用。仅使用179,067个预训练样本（即不到先前强大单细胞基础模型所用数据量的0.5%），scKITE的表现就超越了……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出scKITE模型，在预训练阶段通过轻量级辅助解码器将细胞注释和基因调控等生物学知识注入Transformer编码器，仅用不到0.5%的数据量即超越现有单细胞基础模型，证明生物学知识是超越数据规模的新型扩展维度。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes scKITE, which injects biological knowledge (cell-level text annotations and gene-level regulatory information) into a Transformer encoder via lightweight auxiliary decoders during pretraining, outperforming existing single-cell foundation models with less than 0.5% of the pretraining data and demonstrating that biological knowledge provides a new scaling dimension beyond data size.
